cards.front: What is the most common type of kidney stone, and which conditions favor it?
cards.back: **Calcium oxalate**: radiopaque, with **envelope** or dumbbell crystals. Risk factors: **hypercalciuria**, **Crohn disease** or other fat malabsorption (more oxalate is absorbed from the gut), and **ethylene glycol** poisoning.
cards.back_pt: **Oxalato de cálcio**: radiopaco, com cristais em **envelope** ou em halteres. Fatores de risco: **hipercalciúria**, **doença de Crohn** ou outra má absorção de gordura (mais oxalato é absorvido no intestino) e intoxicação por **etilenoglicol**.

cards.back: **Urease**-producing bacteria (**Proteus**, Klebsiella) split urea into **ammonia**, which makes the urine **alkaline**. Magnesium ammonium phosphate then precipitates as **coffin-lid** crystals. These stones can fill the renal pelvis as **staghorn calculi**.
cards.back_pt: Bactérias produtoras de **urease** (**Proteus**, Klebsiella) quebram a ureia em **amônia**, o que torna a urina **alcalina**. O fosfato de amônio e magnésio então precipita em cristais em **tampa de caixão** (*coffin-lid*). Esses cálculos podem ocupar a pelve renal como **cálculos coraliformes** (*staghorn*).

cards.front: Which kidney stone is radiolucent on plain x-ray, and what favors it?
cards.back: **Uric acid** stones (seen on CT, not on plain film). They form in **acidic urine**. Risk factors: **gout**, high cell turnover (**leukemia**, tumor lysis) and dehydration. Crystals are **rhomboid** or rosette-shaped.
cards.back_pt: Cálculos de **ácido úrico** (visíveis na TC, não na radiografia simples). Formam-se em **urina ácida**. Fatores de risco: **gota**, alta renovação celular (**leucemia**, lise tumoral) e desidratação. Os cristais são **romboides** ou em roseta.

cards.front: What causes cystine stones, and how do their crystals look?
cards.back: **Cystinuria**: an autosomal recessive defect of the **proximal tubule** transporter for dibasic amino acids (**cystine, ornithine, lysine, arginine**). Poorly soluble cystine forms **hexagonal** crystals and stones from childhood. Stones are only faintly radiopaque.
cards.back_pt: **Cistinúria**: defeito autossômico recessivo do transportador do **túbulo proximal** para aminoácidos dibásicos (**cistina, ornitina, lisina, arginina**). A cistina, pouco solúvel, forma cristais **hexagonais** e cálculos desde a infância. Os cálculos são apenas discretamente radiopacos.

cards.front: How does autosomal recessive PKD differ from autosomal dominant PKD?
cards.back: **ADPKD**: adults; **PKD1** (chromosome 16) or **PKD2** (chromosome 4); large cystic kidneys, hypertension, liver cysts, **berry aneurysms**. **ARPKD**: infants; **PKHD1**; oligohydramnios with **Potter sequence** and **congenital hepatic fibrosis**.
cards.back_pt: **DRPAD**: adultos; **PKD1** (cromossomo 16) ou **PKD2** (cromossomo 4); rins grandes e císticos, hipertensão, cistos hepáticos, **aneurismas saculares** (*berry*). **DRPAR**: lactentes; **PKHD1**; oligoidrâmnio com **sequência de Potter** e **fibrose hepática congênita**.

cards.front: Which hormones can renal cell carcinoma secrete as paraneoplastic syndromes?
What are the key features of Wilms tumor?
cards.back: The most common kidney cancer of **young children**. It presents as a large, unilateral, palpable **flank mass**. Linked to loss of **WT1** (chromosome 11p13). **WAGR** syndrome: **W**ilms tumor, **A**niridia, **G**enitourinary anomalies, **R**ange of developmental delays (intellectual disability).
cards.back_pt: O câncer renal mais comum em **crianças pequenas**. Apresenta-se como **massa em flanco** grande, unilateral e palpável. Ligado à perda do **WT1** (cromossomo 11p13). Síndrome **WAGR**: tumor de **W**ilms, **A**niridia, anomalias **G**eniturinárias e atraso do desenvolvimento (*Range of developmental delays*; deficiência intelectual).

cards.front: What do a positive leukocyte esterase and a positive nitrite mean on urine dipstick?
cards.back: **Leukocyte esterase**: white cells in the urine (**pyuria**). **Nitrite**: gram-negative bacteria (e.g., **E. coli**) that convert nitrate to nitrite. Gram-positive causes, such as **Enterococcus** and **S. saprophyticus**, usually give a negative nitrite.
cards.back_pt: **Esterase leucocitária**: leucócitos na urina (**piúria**). **Nitrito**: bactérias gram-negativas (ex.: **E. coli**) que convertem nitrato em nitrito. Causas gram-positivas, como **Enterococcus** e **S. saprophyticus**, geralmente dão nitrito negativo.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has had several urinary tract infections over the past year. She now has dull right flank pain. Urine pH is 8.0. Urine microscopy shows rectangular crystals shaped like coffin lids. CT shows a large branching stone that fills the right renal pelvis and calyces. Urine culture grows a gram-negative rod that spreads in waves across the blood agar plate (swarming motility). Which organism is most likely?
questions.explanation: **Proteus mirabilis** makes **urease**, which splits urea into ammonia and makes the urine **alkaline**. Magnesium ammonium phosphate (**struvite**) then precipitates and can form a **staghorn calculus**; swarming motility is a classic Proteus feature. **E. coli** is the most common cause of UTI overall, but it does not make urease, so it does not cause alkaline urine or struvite stones.
questions.explanation_pt: O **Proteus mirabilis** produz **urease**, que quebra a ureia em amônia e torna a urina **alcalina**. O fosfato de amônio e magnésio (**estruvita**) então precipita e pode formar um **cálculo coraliforme**; a motilidade em ondas (*swarming*) é típica do Proteus. A **E. coli** é a causa mais comum de ITU em geral, mas não produz urease, por isso não causa urina alcalina nem cálculos de estruvita.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has high blood pressure and intermittent flank pain. His mother started dialysis at age 50. Blood pressure is 158/98 mm Hg. Large, irregular masses are palpable in both flanks. Urinalysis shows red blood cells. Ultrasound shows two enlarged kidneys filled with many cysts, and several cysts in the liver. This patient is also at increased risk of which complication?
choices: Congenital hepatic fibrosis with portal hypertension
Subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured saccular aneurysm
questions.explanation: Bilateral enlarged cystic kidneys, hypertension, liver cysts and an affected parent suggest **autosomal dominant PKD** (PKD1 or PKD2). These patients have more **berry (saccular) aneurysms** in the circle of Willis, which can rupture and cause **subarachnoid hemorrhage**. **Congenital hepatic fibrosis** belongs to **autosomal recessive PKD**, which presents in infants; the liver cysts of ADPKD usually do not impair liver function.
questions.explanation_pt: Rins aumentados e císticos bilateralmente, hipertensão, cistos hepáticos e um genitor afetado sugerem **doença renal policística autossômica dominante** (PKD1 ou PKD2). Esses pacientes têm mais **aneurismas saculares** (*berry*) no polígono de Willis, que podem romper e causar **hemorragia subaracnóidea**. A **fibrose hepática congênita** é da **forma autossômica recessiva**, que se apresenta em lactentes; os cistos hepáticos da DRPAD em geral não prejudicam a função hepática.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has 2 months of blood in his urine and dull left flank pain. He has lost weight. He has smoked one pack a day for 40 years, and his BMI is 34 kg/m2. Exam shows a palpable left flank mass and a left scrotal varicocele that does not decrease when he lies down. Hemoglobin is 19.2 g/dL (normal 13.5-17.5). CT shows a solid left renal mass that extends into the left renal vein. Which genetic change is most likely present in the tumor cells?
questions.explanation: Hematuria, flank pain and a flank mass in an older smoker point to **clear cell renal cell carcinoma**. Tumor **EPO** explains the high hemoglobin, and tumor in the **left renal vein** blocks drainage of the left gonadal vein, causing a varicocele that does not empty when supine. Clear cell RCC is linked to loss of **VHL on 3p**, which lets HIF build up and drive VEGF and EPO. **WT1** loss causes Wilms tumor, a tumor of young children.
questions.explanation_pt: Hematúria, dor e massa em flanco em um tabagista mais velho apontam para **carcinoma renal de células claras**. A **EPO** produzida pelo tumor explica a hemoglobina alta, e o tumor na **veia renal esquerda** bloqueia a drenagem da veia gonadal esquerda, causando uma varicocele que não esvazia em decúbito. O carcinoma renal de células claras está ligado à perda do **VHL no 3p**, o que deixa o HIF acumular e estimular VEGF e EPO. A perda do **WT1** causa o tumor de Wilms, um tumor de crianças pequenas.

questions.stem: A 57-year-old man has had three episodes of red urine in the past month. He has no pain with urination and no flank pain. He has never smoked. For 25 years he worked in a factory that made rubber and industrial dyes. Urine culture is negative. Cystoscopy shows a papillary mass on the bladder wall, and biopsy shows malignant urothelial cells. Which exposure most likely contributed to this tumor?
questions.explanation: **Painless hematuria** with a papillary bladder tumor is **urothelial carcinoma**. **Aromatic amines** (e.g., 2-naphthylamine, benzidine) used in the dye and rubber industries are classic occupational causes; **smoking** is the most common risk factor overall. **Benzene** is also an aromatic chemical, but it damages the bone marrow and causes **acute myeloid leukemia**, not bladder cancer. Chronic **Schistosoma haematobium** infection is linked to **squamous cell** carcinoma of the bladder instead.
questions.explanation_pt: **Hematúria indolor** com tumor vesical papilar é **carcinoma urotelial**. As **aminas aromáticas** (ex.: 2-naftilamina, benzidina) usadas nas indústrias de corantes e de borracha são causas ocupacionais clássicas; o **tabagismo** é o fator de risco mais comum em geral. O **benzeno** também é um composto aromático, mas lesa a medula óssea e causa **leucemia mieloide aguda**, não câncer de bexiga. A infecção crônica por **Schistosoma haematobium** está ligada ao carcinoma **de células escamosas** da bexiga.

notes.title: Kidney stones, cystic disease, urinary tract tumors and UTI
notes.body_md:
## Kidney stones

- **Renal colic**: sudden, severe, wave-like flank pain that spreads to the groin, often with **hematuria**. A stone that blocks the ureter causes **hydronephrosis** (dilated pelvis and calyces).
- **Calcium oxalate**: most common; radiopaque; hypercalciuria, Crohn disease, ethylene glycol.
- **Calcium phosphate**: radiopaque; forms in **alkaline** urine.
- **Struvite**: **urease** bacteria (Proteus), alkaline urine, **staghorn calculi**.
- **Uric acid**: **radiolucent**; acidic urine, gout, leukemia.
- **Cystine**: **hexagonal** crystals; cystinuria (cystine, ornithine, lysine, arginine).
- Prevention for all: plenty of **fluids**; **citrate** inhibits calcium stones and alkalinizes urine.

## Cystic kidney disease

- **ADPKD**: adults; PKD1/PKD2; large kidneys, hypertension, liver cysts, **berry aneurysms**.
- **ARPKD**: infants; PKHD1; Potter sequence, **congenital hepatic fibrosis**.
- **Medullary sponge kidney**: dilated medullary collecting ducts; stones and infection, usually with normal kidney function.

## Tumors

- **Renal cell carcinoma**: clear cells from the **proximal tubule**; **VHL** (3p); smoking and obesity. Hematuria, flank pain and mass. Paraneoplastic **EPO, renin, PTHrP, ACTH**. Grows into the **renal vein** and IVC.
- **Wilms tumor**: young children; flank mass; **WT1**; **WAGR**.
- **Urothelial carcinoma**: **painless hematuria**; **smoking**, **aromatic amines**, cyclophosphamide. **Schistosoma haematobium** is linked to **squamous cell** carcinoma.

## Urinary tract infection

- **E. coli** is the most common cause. Others: **Proteus**, **Klebsiella**, Enterococcus and **S. saprophyticus** (young sexually active women).
- **Cystitis**: dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain; usually no fever.
- **Pyelonephritis**: fever, **flank pain**, costovertebral angle tenderness; **WBC casts**.
- Dipstick: **leukocyte esterase** (pyuria) and **nitrite** (gram-negative bacteria).
- **Sterile pyuria** (pyuria with a negative culture): think of **Chlamydia**, gonorrhea or tuberculosis.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Cálculos renais

- **Cólica renal**: dor em flanco súbita, intensa e em ondas, que irradia para a virilha, frequentemente com **hematúria**. Um cálculo que obstrui o ureter causa **hidronefrose** (pelve e cálices dilatados).
- **Oxalato de cálcio**: o mais comum; radiopaco; hipercalciúria, doença de Crohn, etilenoglicol.
- **Fosfato de cálcio**: radiopaco; forma-se em urina **alcalina**.
- **Estruvita**: bactérias produtoras de **urease** (Proteus), urina alcalina, **cálculos coraliformes**.
- **Ácido úrico**: **radiotransparente**; urina ácida, gota, leucemia.
- **Cistina**: cristais **hexagonais**; cistinúria (cistina, ornitina, lisina, arginina).
- Prevenção para todos: muita **hidratação**; o **citrato** inibe cálculos de cálcio e alcaliniza a urina.

## Doença renal cística

- **DRPAD**: adultos; PKD1/PKD2; rins grandes, hipertensão, cistos hepáticos, **aneurismas saculares**.
- **DRPAR**: lactentes; PKHD1; sequência de Potter, **fibrose hepática congênita**.
- **Rim esponja medular**: ductos coletores medulares dilatados; cálculos e infecção, em geral com função renal normal.

## Tumores

- **Carcinoma de células renais**: células claras do **túbulo proximal**; **VHL** (3p); tabagismo e obesidade. Hematúria, dor e massa em flanco. Paraneoplásicas: **EPO, renina, PTHrP, ACTH**. Invade a **veia renal** e a veia cava inferior.
- **Tumor de Wilms**: crianças pequenas; massa em flanco; **WT1**; **WAGR**.
- **Carcinoma urotelial**: **hematúria indolor**; **tabagismo**, **aminas aromáticas**, ciclofosfamida. O **Schistosoma haematobium** está ligado ao carcinoma **de células escamosas**.

## Infecção do trato urinário

- A **E. coli** é a causa mais comum. Outras: **Proteus**, **Klebsiella**, Enterococcus e **S. saprophyticus** (mulheres jovens sexualmente ativas).
- **Cistite**: disúria, polaciúria, urgência, dor suprapúbica; em geral sem febre.
- **Pielonefrite**: febre, **dor em flanco**, dor à punho-percussão lombar (sinal de Giordano positivo); **cilindros leucocitários**.
- Fita reagente: **esterase leucocitária** (piúria) e **nitrito** (bactérias gram-negativas).
- **Piúria estéril** (piúria com cultura negativa): pensar em **Chlamydia**, gonorreia ou tuberculose.
